'''Jane Catherine Ngila''' is the head of the Chemical Sciences Department at the [[University of Johannesburg]], her work focuses on applying [[nanotechnology]] for water purification. She was the Acting Executive Director of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] and member of the [[Academy of Science of South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.assaf.org.za/index.php/about-assaf/members#C | title=Members | publisher=[[Academy of Science of South Africa]] | accessdate=17 October 2017}}</ref>

==Career==
Ngila obtained her [[Bachelor of Education|B.Ed.]] in 1986 and [[Master of Science|M.Sc.]] in chemistry in 1992 from [[Kenyatta University]] in [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]].<ref name="Ngila_1">{{cite web | url=https://mg.co.za/article/2016-08-15-00-professor-jane-catherine-ngila-specialist-in-nanotechnology-for-water-treatment | title=Professor Jane Catherine Ngila: Specialist in nanotechnology for water treatment | publisher=Mail Guardian | date=15 August 2016 | accessdate=17 October 2017}}</ref> She was awarded a scholarship, AIDAB/EMSS scholarship, by the Australian government.<ref name="Ngila_2">{{Cite web |title=Jane Ngila - University of Johannesburg |url=https://pure.uj.ac.za/en/persons/jane-ngila/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=University of Johannesburg |language=en}}</ref> Ngila obtained her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in analytical-environmental chemistry from the [[University of New South Wales]], [[Australia]] in 1996. She started her career as a tutor in the chemistry department at [[Kenyatta University]] in 1989, and was appointed as a lecturer in 1996. She later worked at the [[University of Botswana]] (1998–2006) and then as a senior lecturer at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] (2006–2011) before being appointed a professorship of applied chemistry at the [[University of Johannesburg]] in 2011.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://aasciences.ac.ke/fellow/ngila-jane-catherine|title=Ngila Jane Catherine {{!}} The AAS|website=aasciences.ac.ke|access-date=2019-06-26}}</ref><ref name="Ngila_1" /> Ngila has been a deputy director at the Morendat Institute of Oil & Gas (MIOG), [[Kenya Pipeline Company]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://morendat.azurewebsites.net/administration/|title=Prof. Jane Catherine Ngila, Riara University (Nurturing Innovators)|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-26|archive-date=26 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626190613/https://morendat.azurewebsites.net/administration/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ngila serves as a [[United Nations University|UNU]] council member and is the executive director of the African Foundation for Women and Youth in Education, Science, Technology and Innovation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jane Catherine Ngila |url=https://unu.edu/about/unu-council-member/jane-catherine-ngila |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=United Nations University |language=en}}</ref> In 2025 she was a vice-President of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] and its governing council led by Prof [[Lise Korsten]].<ref name="aas">{{Cite web |title=The African Academy of Sciences (AAS) |url=https://aasciences.africa/governing-council |access-date=2025-09-06 |website=aasciences.africa |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Ngila's work is in the field of analytical environmental chemistry; her research interests include monitoring water quality/pollution and water purification using [[Resin|chemical resins]] and other [[Adsorption|adsorbents]].<ref name="Ngila_2" /> Ngila is an author or co-author of over 150 papers and review articles. Her current [[h-index]] is 38.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/12048815|title=Ngila, Jane Catherine - Web of Science Researcher Profile|website=www.webofscience.com|access-date=2026-10-28|date=|url-status=live}}</ref>
